title: HTTP/3 WebSocket Handler Exception Close Policy Architecture
purpose: Define configurable close status and reason policy for unexpected accepted WebSocket handler exceptions.
design_summary: `Http3ServerOptions.WebSocketHandlerExceptionCloseStatusCode` and `WebSocketHandlerExceptionCloseReason` let server owners configure the best-effort fallback close frame used when an accepted RFC 9220 WebSocket tunnel handler throws an unexpected non-cancellation, non-QUIC exception. The server validates the configured close payload at startup and uses it in the existing handler-exception catch path after emitting diagnostics when no dynamic close-policy selector is configured or selected.
data_and_state_considerations: The policy is captured when the server starts and is request-stream scoped when applied. It does not inspect arbitrary exception types, mutate connection state, or change handlers that explicitly close their own tunnels.
edge_cases_and_constraints: The default remains 1011 with reason `internal error`.
Invalid close status codes or oversized reasons are rejected before the listener is exposed to callers.
Per-exception dynamic mapping is trace-owned by `ARC-QUIC-RFC9220-0014`.
risks: Overly specific close reasons can expose application detail, so applications should choose configured reasons deliberately.
External peer behavior still needs live interoperability proof before promoting beyond local loopback evidence.
